macros.VExactStrictText: The exact check was tried on 942 entries (every hyperstatic certificate, and the entries marked provably optimal that the isostatic certificate does not cover); for 62 of them the coordinates or the inner products were recognised as exact, and 39 of these are confirmed, each in at most 679 seconds of CPU time. For the other 23 it gives no answer: for 20, the uniform stress is not an equilibrium stress (the exact search for another one covers only rational coordinates); for 2 ($(22,891)$, $(23,552)$), the rigidity matrix does not fit the memory limit; for 1 ($(17,64)$), no exact positive stress was found. Of the confirmed entries, $(16,288)$, $(21,162)$, $(22,275)$ are above the size limit of the census rule; for them this is the only certificate, and Table~\ref{tab:census} counts them as strict.
macros.VNonoptText: Proposition~\ref{prop:nonopt} applies to $(3,576)$ at $\tau=10^{-10}, 10^{-9}, 10^{-8}, 10^{-7}$ ($Q^*$ within $1.3\cdot10^{-8}$ of the stored code; smallest relative stress $-1.1\cdot10^{-6}$) and $(3,791)$ at $\tau=10^{-7}$ ($Q^*$ within $7.4\cdot10^{-5}$ of the stored code; a configuration rather far from the code; smallest relative stress $-6.2$).
macros.VNStrictNewSentence: \emph{Two more are strict local minima}, $(10,238)$, $(12,210)$, by Theorem~\ref{thm:main} checked in exact arithmetic, where the census subsystem had failed;
macros.VNFamilyItem: \emph{Four remain undecided}: $(22,47)$, $(22,48)$, $(23,50)$, which the table notes as members of continuous families of codes without rattlers, and our numerical analysis agrees (one infinitesimal flex, on which $H_\omega$ vanishes); and $(19,166)$.
macros.VUndecidedSentence: Finally, the exact core of $(19,166)$ is bar-rigid, with 4{,}875 contacts, but numerically no stress is positive on every contact (the largest smallest entry of a stress of total one is $4.6\cdot10^{-17}$ in absolute value), and the 3{,}810 contacts that carry stress fail our test for bar-rigidity (rank 2{,}022 modulo $q$ against 2{,}394 needed), so the first-order criterion does not apply; it remains open.
